rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab usage treats consulting a bird as an omen from its flight, good or bad; the cited poetry illustrates this divinatory idiom.
rows.anchor: قال وقولهم سألت الطير وقلت للطير إنما هو زجرتها من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bird is placed at the neck because deeds stay attached like a collar; Arabic also uses body parts for the whole person.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال طائره في عنقه ولم يقل في يده لينبه على لزوم ذلك له

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Saying someone's neck or throat is free emancipates them because it means the whole body; saying hand or hair is free does not.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: إذا قال الإنسان عنقك أو رقبتك حر عتق

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: He treats such expressions alike and says either declaration emancipates.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: هما سواء يعتق في الحالين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafsika is the subject of kafa and hasiban is accusative as specification; al-Sarraj instead posits an omitted subject and parses hasiban as circumstantial.
rows.anchor: موضع بنفسك رفع لأنه فاعل كفى وحسيبا نصب على التمييز له

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He explains the bird as a person's good or ill omen; the verse echoes bird-omen expressions in the messengers' story and Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: وقيل طائره يمنه وشؤمه عن الحسن وهو ما يتطير منه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والقتيبي
rows.claim: They understand the bird as a person's share of good and evil.
rows.anchor: وقيل طائره حظه من الخير والشر عن أبي عبدة والقتيبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the bird to mean the book of deeds; another says each person is his own guide and witness.
rows.anchor: وقيل طائره كتابه وقيل معناه جعلنا لكل إنسان دليلا من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record is written by guardian angels and presented open for its owner to see and read; the pronoun 'for him' can refer to the person or the deed.
rows.anchor: وهو ما كتبه الحفظة عليهم من أعمالهم { يلقاه } أي يرى ذلك الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative is elliptical for 'it will be said to him: read your book'; Qatada says even the previously illiterate will read.
rows.anchor: ها هنا حذف أي ويقال له اقرأ كتابك قال قتادة يقرأ يومئذ

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A person will recall all recorded deeds as if doing them at that moment, explaining the comparison with the record in al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: وروى جابر بن خالد بن نجيح عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: يذكر العبد جميع أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing every deed and its just recompense leaves no defense and shows the gathered people that God wrongs no one; al-Hasan praises this fairness.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن يا ابن آدم لقد أنصفك من جعلك حسيب نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits its follower, straying harms its follower, and no bearer carries another's sin.
rows.anchor: أي من اهتدى في الدنيا إلى دين الله وطاعته فمنفعة اهتدائه راجعة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is not punished for another person's sins.
rows.anchor: أي لا تحمل حاملة حمل أخرى أي ثقل ذنوب غيرها ولا يعاقب أحد

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet's saying that one's right hand does not bend over one's left is offered as an analogy for personal responsibility.
rows.anchor: " لا تحن يمينك على شمالك "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the claim that children of unbelievers are punished in Hell along with their parents.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة واضحة على بطلان قول من يقول إن أطفال الكفار يعذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view limits the promise to annihilating punishment: messengers must first warn and excuse people fully, though rational obligations may be punishable.
rows.anchor: وما كنا معذبين قوما بعذاب الاستئصال إلا بعد الإعذار إليهم والإنذار لهم

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes, and the author's preferred reading, deny punishment before a messenger is sent for obligations known through revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال الأكثرون من المفسرين وهو الأصح أن المراد بالآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, rational knowledge of God may be punishable without revelation, though God refrains from this through generosity; messengers join reason and revelation as proof.
rows.anchor: إذا اجتمع داعي العقل وداعي السمع تأكد الأمر وزال الريب

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The common reading has amarnā with light hamza and no lengthening; Yaʿqub, Ali, al-Hasan, Abu al-Aliyah, and Qatada lengthen it.
rows.anchor: القراءة العامة أمرنا بالتخفيف غير ممدود وقرأ يعقوب آمرنا بالمد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو عثمان النهدي وأبو جعفر محمد بن علي
rows.claim: They read ammarna with doubled mīm; al-Hasan and Yahya ibn Yaʿmar read with kasra on mīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أمرنا بالتشديد للميم ابن عباس وأبو عثمان النهدي وأبو جعفر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: He explains amarnā as 'We made numerous,' citing Labid's verse and the verb for a people becoming numerous.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد أمرنا أكثرنا من قولهم أمر بنو فلان أي كثروا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: If the light form does not mean becoming numerous, it means God commanded obedience and the people disobeyed; he rejects making them rulers because a town would not have many rulers.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: لا يخلو قوله أمرنا مخففة الهمزة من أن يكون فعلنا من الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A command to obey cannot be exclusive to the affluent, since God commands all people; the commentary links this to leaving lands overrun by sin.
rows.anchor: فقد أمر الله بطاعته جميع خلقه من مترف وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutraf means someone left in luxury to do as he pleases; tadmīr means destruction and madhūr means driven away.
rows.anchor: الترفّه النعمة قال ابن عرفة المترف المتروك يصنع ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kam is accusative with ahlakna; the bāʾ in 'by your Lord' is for praise and is nominative in force.
rows.anchor: كم أهلكنا موضع كم نصب بأهلكنا ودخلت الباء في قولك بربك للمدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuslīhā is circumstantial, and 'for whom We will' apposes the preceding clause; the pronoun repeats because the apposition is another clause.
rows.anchor: ويصليها في موضع نصب على الحال لمن نريد بدل من قوله: { عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred first interpretation is that after proof and messengers God repeatedly commands town leaders to obey; they persist in sin, the warning becomes due, and the town is destroyed.
rows.anchor: أمرنا مترفيها أي رؤساءها وساداتها بالطاعة واتباع الرسل أمرا بعد أمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: They gloss the command as an order to obey, which the people disobeyed and thereby became corrupt.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير أن معناه أمرناهم بالطاعة فعصوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affluent are singled out because others follow their leaders, so an order to them also reaches their followers.
rows.anchor: وإنما خص المترفين وهم المنعمون والرؤساء بالذكر لأن غيرهم تبع لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation makes the clause describe a town already commanded; the conditional's answer is implicit in the context.
rows.anchor: ثانيها: أن قوله: { أمرنا مترفيها } من صفة القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the first interpretation when the reading means command; lengthened or doubled readings require one of the other views.
rows.anchor: والوجه الأول عندي أصح الوجوه وأقربها إلى الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second view leaves the conditional's answer unstated because context supplies it; a Qur'anic example and a Hudhayli poem support omission.
rows.anchor: فلم يأت لإذا جواب في طول الكلام للاستغناء عنه بما في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view reverses the order: after the town's leaders disobey God's command, He wills their destruction.
rows.anchor: ثالثها: أن الآية محمولة على التقديم والتأخير وتقديرها إذا أمرنا مترفي قرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth reads 'when We will' figuratively as imminent destruction and certain knowledge of it.
rows.anchor: ورابعها: أنه سبحانه ذكر الإرادة على وجه المجاز والاتساع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many nations after Noah were destroyed; kam indicates abundance, whereas rub indicates scarcity.
rows.anchor: فقال { وكم أهلكنا من القرون } أي من الأمم الكثيرة المكذبة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
rows.claim: He defines a generation as 120 years.
rows.anchor: والقرن مائة وعشرون سنة عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى

rows.speaker: محمد بن القاسم المازني
rows.claim: He defines a generation as 100 years; this is also reported as a Prophetic narration.
rows.anchor: وقيل مائة سنة عن محمد بن القاسم المازني وروي ذلك مرفوعا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He defines a generation as 80 years; Ibn Sirin reports 40 years as a Prophetic narration.
rows.anchor: وقيل ثمانون سنة عن الكلبي وقيل أربعون سنة ورواه ابن سيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows and sees the servants' sins and will requite them without anything escaping Him.
rows.anchor: أي كفى ربك عالما بذنوب خلقه { بصيرا } بها يجازيهم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immediate world is named for its short-lived quality; God grants only what He wills to whom He wills and may restrict the worldly seeker.
rows.anchor: أي النعم العاجلة وهي الدنيا فعبر عنها بصفتها { عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly seeker enters Hell blamed and excluded from God's mercy.
rows.anchor: { مذموما } ملوما { مدحورا } مبعدا من رحمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Work done for worldly reward alone, without seeking God or the hereafter, earns only the worldly portion God wills and no afterlife reward; the gift may be misused and punished.
rows.anchor: معنى الآية من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا بعمله الذي افترضه الله عليه لا يريد به وجه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking the hereafter requires obedience, avoiding sins, and belief in God's unity and messengers; the effort is accepted.
rows.anchor: أي فعل الطاعات وتجنب المعاصي وهو مع ذلك مصدق بتوحيد الله مقر بأنبيائه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says God's gratitude consists in multiplying good deeds and overlooking sins.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة والمعنى أنا أحللنا سعيهم محل ما يشكر عليه في حسن الجزاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He urges pursuit of the hereafter: its seeker attains it and may also gain the world, while a worldly seeker may fail at both.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قال: اطلبوا الآخرة فما رأيت طالبا لها إلا نالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplies both groups; the world is given to righteous and wicked alike, but the hereafter belongs to the pious and provision is not withheld for unbelief or sin.
rows.anchor: أي كل واحد من هذين الفريقين ممن يريد الدنيا وممن يريد الآخرة نمدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may seek both rewards if immediate gain is secondary, as with a fighter who seeks to honor religion and treats spoils as incidental.
rows.anchor: نعم إذا جعل العاجل تبعا للآجل كالمجاهد في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly differences include wealth and poverty, master and slave, health and illness; the afterlife has greater ranks earned in proportion to deeds.
rows.anchor: بأن جعلنا بعضهم أغنياء وبعضهم فقراء وبعضهم موالي وبعضهم عبيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report likens the distance between Paradise's highest and lowest ranks to the distance between heaven and earth; obedience increases afterlife rank, not worldly provision.
rows.anchor: قد روي أن ما بين أعلى درجات الجنة وأسفلها ما بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be to the Prophet with his community intended, or to any hearer; it forbids association in belief, worship, desire, or fear.
rows.anchor: قيل إن الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد به أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Association leaves one condemned and abandoned; sitting can mean humiliation, defeat, or incapacity rather than literal sitting.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى القعود الذل والخزي والخسران والعجز لا الجلوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage connects to punishment after messengers and persistent disobedience, or to the earlier story of Israel's two judgments.
rows.anchor: وجه اتصال الآية الأولى بما قبلها أنها اتصلت بقوله: { حتى يبعث رسولا }

rows.speaker: الكوفي غير عاصم
rows.claim: They read yablughā with dual alif and nūn kasra; the others read yablughanna.
rows.anchor: القراءة: يبلغان بالألف وكسر النون كوفي غير عاصم والباقون يبلغن

rows.speaker: المكي والشامي ويعقوب وسهل
rows.claim: They read uff with fatḥa here and in al-Anbiyāʾ and al-Aḥqāf.
rows.anchor: أف بفتح الفاء ها هنا وفي الأنبياء والأحقاف مكي شامي ويعقوب

rows.speaker: المدني وحفص والباقون
rows.claim: Medina and Hafs read uff with kasra and tanwīn; the others use kasra without tanwīn. Abu al-Sammak and Ibn Abbas have additional noncanonical forms.
rows.anchor: وأف بالكسر والتنوين في الجميع مدني وحفص والباقون أف بالكسر غير منون

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The dual alif merely marks the dual, since aḥaduhumā already identifies the parents; al-Zajjaj instead calls it an appositive.
rows.anchor: والذكر الذي عاد من قوله: { أحدهما } يغني عن إثبات علامة الضمير

rows.speaker: أبو علي والزجاج
rows.claim: Uff has several forms; fatḥa is built like sarʿān, tanwīn marks indefiniteness, and no tanwīn makes a definite exclamation.
rows.anchor: من قرأ أف بالفتح فإنه بناه على الفتح كقولهم سرعان ذا إهالة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He has a noncanonical reading with kasra in al-dhull; the word with the other vocalization means disgrace rather than gentle submission.
rows.anchor: وجناح الذل بكسر الذال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kindness-to-parents phrase is governed by qaḍā or an implied 'He enjoined'; kāf in 'as they raised me' means corresponding to their care, or according to al-Akhfash 'because of.'
rows.anchor: العامل في الباء قضى والتقدير وقضى بالوالدين إحسانا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They explain qaḍā as an emphatic command; al-Rabi says obligation and Mujahid says testament.
rows.anchor: أي أمر ربك أمرا باتا عن ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative command means God wills sincere worship of Himself and disapproves worship of another; old age is singled out because parents need service then like dependent children.
rows.anchor: أراد منكم عبادته على وجه الإخلاص وكره منكم عبادة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Old age is singled out because parents need more tending and service then, like dependent children; the comparison also recalls Jesus speaking in the cradle and as an adult.
rows.anchor: وخص حال الكبر وإن كان من الواجب طاعة الوالدين على كل حال لأن الحاجة أكثر في تلك الحال إلى التعهد والخدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to Jesus speaking in the cradle and as an adult highlights his survival to old age; the day of judgment is singled out because only God rules then.
rows.anchor: أخبر أن عيسى يكلم الناس في المهد وأنه يعيش حتى يكهل

rows.speaker: علي بن موسى الرضا
rows.claim: A report through his forefathers says God would have forbidden even a shorter word than uff if one existed.
rows.anchor: روي عن علي بن موسى الرضا عن أبيه عن جده أبي عبد الله ع قال: لو علم الله لفظة

rows.speaker: علي بن موسى الرضا
rows.claim: Another report calls uff the least disobedience and says an even easier expression would also be forbidden.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه قال أدنى العقوق أف ولو علم الله شيئا أيسر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Do not recoil from aged incontinent parents; tend them as they tended the child.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد معناه إن بلغا عندك من الكبر ما يبولان ويحدثان

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda explains uff and tuff as fingertip grime; Ibn Abbas calls uff an expression of aversion, and another gloss says foul odor.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الأف والتف وسخ الأصابع إذا فتلته عن أبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proverb praises the vulture because its young feed it in old age.
rows.anchor: وجاء في المثل أبر من النسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the old age refer to the addressee reaching adulthood while one or both parents remain.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الكبر في الآية راجع إلى المخاطب أي إن بلغت حال الكبر وهو حال التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not rebuke parents harshly or shout; another interpretation says not to refuse what they ask, as in the command about the supplicant.
rows.anchor: أي لا تزجرهما بإغلاظ وصياح وقيل معناه لا تمتنع من شيء أراده منك

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: A gracious word is like the speech of a sinful servant addressing a severe master.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه قل لهما قول العبد المذنب للسيد الفظ الغليظ عن سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing means active humility in word and deed, gentle submission rather than humiliation, like a bird sheltering its young.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالذل ها هنا اللين والتواضع دون الهوان من خفض الطائر جناحه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Look at parents compassionately, do not raise voice or hands above theirs, and do not walk ahead of them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله ع: معناه لا تملأ عينيك من النظر إليهما إلا برأفة ورحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pray for mercy for believing parents in life and after death as recompense for raising you; this indicates a child's prayer for deceased parents is heard.
rows.anchor: ادع لهما بالمغفرة والرحمة في حياتهما وبعد مماتهما جزاء لتربيتهما إياك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report warns three times of shame on anyone whose parent reaches old age while the person still fails to enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: قالوا من يا رسول الله قال: " من أدرك أبويه عند الكبر

rows.speaker: أبو أسيد الأنصاري
rows.claim: He asks the Prophet whether any filial duty remains after a parent's death.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو أسيد الأنصاري قال بينما نحن عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report answers that after parents die one may pray for them, seek forgiveness, fulfill commitments, honor their friends, and maintain dependent kinship ties.
rows.anchor: نعم الصلاة عليهما والاستغفار لهما وإنفاذ عهدهما من بعدهما

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says people have been taught and commanded to adopt God's teaching and discipline.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة هكذا علمتم وبهذا أمرتم فخذوه بتعليم الله وأدبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the devotion or disobedience in people's hearts and forgives a lapse without inward disobedience; he prefers that God knows everything concealed.
rows.anchor: بما تضمرون من البر والعقوق فمن ندرت منه نادرة وهو لا يضمر عقوقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous means obedient to God; awābīn are forgiven.
rows.anchor: { إن تكونوا صالحين } أي طائعين لله

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: They explain awābīn as repentant worshipers returning from sin; Qatada says obedient benefactors.
rows.anchor: والأواب التواب المتعبد الراجع عن ذنبه عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: He identifies them as people who sin and repent repeatedly; Ibn Abbas says they turn back to God in what befalls them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهم الذين يذنبون ثم يتوبون ثم يذنبون ثم يتوبون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another narration he calls awābīn glorifiers, supported by the words to the mountains; another view says they pray between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم المسبحون عن ابن عباس في رواية أخرى

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: He describes a four-unit prayer with fifty recitations of Qul huwa Allahu aḥad in each unit.
rows.anchor: قال صلاة أربع ركعات يقرأ في كل ركعة خمسين مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waste is dispersal and excess for corrupt ends; large spending for reform is not waste. A poet's use of b-dh-r witnesses scattering.
rows.anchor: التبذير التفريق بالإسراف وأصله أن يفرق كما يفرق البذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away may mean aversion, attending to a higher priority, or disdain; the root ḥ-s-r also covers uncovering, grief, exhaustion, and being depleted.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون عن قلى وقد يكون للاشتغال بما هو الأولى وقد يكون للإذلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In wa-immā taʿriḍanna, mā is extra; seeking mercy is either purpose or circumstantial description of hoping for it.
rows.anchor: وأما تعرضن تقديره وإن تعرض وما مزيدة وابتغاء مفعول له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: They say relatives are owed rights God made obligatory in one's property; al-Suddi identifies them as the Prophet's kin.
rows.anchor: واعط القرابات حقوقهم التي أوجبها الله لهم في أموالكم عن ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: السدي وعلي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the kin as the Prophet's family; Ali ibn al-Husayn tells a Syrian captive that they are the kin commanded to receive their due.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن المراد قرابة الرسول عن السدي

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: He reports that when the verse was revealed the Prophet gave Fadak to Fatima; al-Maʾmun later restored it to her descendants.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: لما نزل قوله وآت ذا القربى حقه أعطى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor and stranded traveler also have a due, including zakat and other rights for the poor and aid for a wayfarer cut off from home.
rows.anchor: معناه وآت المسكين حقه الذي جعله الله له من الزكاة وغيرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: They define a spendthrift as someone who spends money on an improper use; Mujahid says one mudd on falsehood is waste but all wealth for a right cause is not.
rows.anchor: قيل إن المبذر الذي ينفق المال في غير حقه عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: He counsels being a reliable mount for believers and avoiding waste.
rows.anchor: أن أمير المؤمنين ع قال لعناية: كن زاملة للمؤمنين وإن خير المطايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasteful people follow Satan's path or are his companions in Hell; Satan has repeatedly been ungrateful to his Lord.
rows.anchor: معناه ان المسرفين أتباع الشياطين سالكون طريقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When unable to give while hoping for future provision, one should promise kindly and speak gently.
rows.anchor: أي لتبتغي الفضل من الله والسعة التي يمكنك معها البذل

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: When asked for something he did not have, the Prophet would say God would provide for him and the requester from His bounty.
rows.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands or constricts provision according to people's circumstances and interests despite ample stores; He knows what benefits each person.
rows.anchor: أي يوسع مرة ويضيق مرة بحسب المصلحة مع سعة خزائنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports generosity, opposes miserliness, and urges measured spending.
rows.anchor: فيها حثا على الإعطاء اعتمادا على الله تعالى ونهيا عن البخل وحتما على القصد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وابن كثير والباقون
rows.claim: They differ on khaṭaʾ: forms include fatḥa, kasra with a long alif, and kasra without lengthening; al-Zuhri, Abu Rajaʾ, and al-Hasan have further variants.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان كان خطأ بفتح الخاء والطاء

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
rows.claim: They read lā tusrif with second-person ta; the others read third-person ya.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم فلا تسرف بالتاء والباقون بالياء

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
rows.claim: They read al-qisṭās with kasra on qāf; the others use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر القسطاس بكسر القاف والباقون بضمها

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Khaṭaʾ is unintended error, but akhṭaʾa and khaṭiʾa can overlap; other readings may be verbal nouns for deliberate sin or missing a target.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي قالوا أخطأ في معنى خطىء كما أن خطىء في معنى أخطأ

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: On yusrif, the implied subject can be the first murderer; killing is excess, and warning him is justified because the victim's guardian or ruler can retaliate.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن يكون القاتل الأول فيكون تقديره فلا يسرف القاتل في القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, yusrif may refer to the victim's guardian, who must not kill anyone beyond the murderer or more people than the murderer killed; Arabs did this.
rows.anchor: والآخر: أن يكون في يسرف ضمير الولي أي فلا يسرف الولي في القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With tusrif, the address may warn any person against unlawful murder or warn the guardian against exceeding retaliation.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ فلا تسرف بالتاء احتمل وجهين أيضا أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The slain person is supported because the guardian can exact the right; if the victim had pardoned, the guardian could not retaliate.
rows.anchor: بدلالة أن المقتول لو أبرىء من السبب المؤدي إلى القتل لم يكن للولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qisṭās and al-qusṭās are dialect variants like qirṭās and qurṭās, with ḍamma more common.
rows.anchor: وأما القسطاس والقسطاس فهما لغتان مثل القرطاس والقرطاس والضم أكثر

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report attributes to adultery six consequences: loss of facial light, reduced provision, and hastened ruin in this life; divine anger, hard reckoning, and Hell in the next.
rows.anchor: في الزنا ست خصال ثلاث في الدنيا وثلاث في الآخرة فأما اللواتي في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A protected life may be taken only for a just cause such as unbelief, apostasy, unjust murder, or adultery while married.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يجب عليه القتل إما لكفره أو ردته أو لأنه قتل نفسا بغير حق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: They say the slain person's guardian may retaliate, take blood money, or pardon; Qatada limits the authority to retaliation.
rows.anchor: سلطان القود على القاتل أو الدية أو العفو عن ابن عباس والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan's property may be approached only in the best way until maturity; the author refers to his commentary on al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: حتى يبلغ أشده } فسرناه في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping a covenant includes the orphan's property and will, all divine commands and prohibitions, and vows that become binding when undertaken; it will be questioned and requited.
rows.anchor: في الوصية بمال اليتيم وغيرها وقيل إن كل ما أمر الله به ونهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete measures and weights and give people their rights; al-qisṭās is a balance, steelyard per al-Hasan, or Persian for justice per Mujahid.
rows.anchor: وهو الميزان صغر أم كبر عن الزجاج وقيل هو القبان عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An upright measure has no shortchanging or cheating; it is better in reward, nearer to God, and worldly proof of trustworthiness, with a better hereafter outcome.
rows.anchor: { المستقيم } الذي لا بخس فيه ولا غبن

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأهل الكوفة والباقون
rows.claim: They differ between annexed masculine sayyiʾuhu and indefinite feminine sayyiʾatan; the annexed reading singles out the evil among previously mentioned acts.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأهل الكوفة كان سيئه بضم الهمزة مضافا إلى الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine reading may treat makrūhan as a substitute or circumstantial predicate; the grammarian rejects the latter because the pronoun is feminine.
rows.anchor: فإنه يجوز أن لا نجعل مكروها صفة لسيئة ولكن نجعله بدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qafw means following someone's tracks; Abu Ubayda also uses it for slander and notes variant forms.
rows.anchor: اللغة: القفو اتباع الأثر ومنه القيافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharq denotes cutting, a generous man, or an open plain; marah is intense joy.
rows.anchor: وأصل الخرق القطع ورجل خرق يتخرق في السخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexical discussion glosses the poetic khāwī al-mukhtaraq as an empty passage and says marah is intense joy.
rows.anchor: وقاتم الأعماق خاوي المخترق أي خاوي المقطع والمرح شدة الفرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'asked about' may refer to the faculties or to the human being; the verse means hearing, sight, and heart are accountable for their use.
rows.anchor: الهاء تعود إلى كل أي يسأل عن استعمال هذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: They say do not claim to have heard, seen, or known what you have not; Hasan says not to backbite, and Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya says it forbids false testimony.
rows.anchor: لا تقل سمعت ولم تسمع ولا رأيت ولم تر ولا علمت ولم تعلم عن ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general rule is to speak, act, and intend only what one knows is permissible and to believe only what one knows may be believed.
rows.anchor: ولا تفعل إلا ما تعلم أنه مما يجوز أن يفعل ولا تعتقد إلا ما تعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some of the author's fellow theologians infer that analogy and solitary reports are impermissible because they do not yield certain knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل جماعة من أصحابنا بهذا على أن العمل بالقياس وبخبر الواحد غير جائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the faculties themselves are questioned; a report from Ibn Abbas says God asks people how they used them.
rows.anchor: قال الوالبي عن ابن عباس: يسأل الله العباد فيما استعملوها

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عن أبي حمزة الثمالي
rows.claim: The Prophet says each person is asked about lifespan, use of the body, source and use of wealth, and love for the Prophet's family.
rows.anchor: لا يزول قدم عبد يوم القيامة بين يدي الله عز وجل حتى يسأله عن أربع خصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking arrogantly means swaggering, pride, and false delight; a person cannot pierce the earth or reach the mountains, so should show humility and dignity.
rows.anchor: معناه لا تمش على وجه الأشر والبطر والخيلاء والتكبر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He glosses the command as not walking arrogantly or boastfully.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج معناه لا تمش في الأرض مختالا فخورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil acts listed earlier are disliked by God, which the author argues against compulsion: one thing cannot be both willed and disliked by Him.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة واضحة على بطلان قول المجبرة فإنه سبحانه صرح بأنه يكره المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These commands and prohibitions are wisdom leading to knowledge of the distinction between good and evil.
rows.anchor: { من الحكمة } المؤدية إلى المعرفة بالحسن والقبح والفرق بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns profession and speech; although addressed to the Prophet, it intends others for stronger admonition.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد به غيره ليكون أبلغ في الزجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Association leads to being cast into Hell, blamed and expelled from divine mercy.
rows.anchor: فتطرح بمعنى أنك إذا فعلت ذلك ألقيت وطرحت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke challenges people who claim God chose sons for them but took daughters for Himself, assigning Himself the supposedly lower share.
rows.anchor: أخلصكم الله سبحانه بالبنين وخصكم بهم واتخذ لنفسه الإناث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim is an enormity because they attribute to God what they would not accept for themselves and call the highest angels female.
rows.anchor: حيث أضفتم إلى الله سبحانه ما لم ترضوا لأنفسكم به وجعلتم الملائكة

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والباقون
rows.claim: They differ between a light and a geminated reading of li-yadhdhakkarū; Abu Ali says it means reflection, not recollection after forgetting.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم ليذكروا ساكنة الذال خفيفة

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام وأبو بكر
rows.claim: They read 'as they say' with third-person ya; Basrans use second-person ta in the first phrase, with other variant combinations reported.
rows.anchor: وقرأ كما يقولون بالياء يسبح له بالياء أهل المدينة والشام وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Above what they say' may be coordinated with the preceding phrase or may independently declare God's transcendence; either ya or ta is sound in 'the heavens glorify.'
rows.anchor: فأما من قرأ سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون فإنه يحتمل وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an repeats proofs and examples so people reflect and recognize truth, yet unbelievers grow more distant and flee.
rows.anchor: أي كررنا الدلائل وفصلنا المعاني والأمثال وغير ذلك مما يوجب الاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation establishes proof, removes excuses, benefits those who respond, and prevents worse corruption among those who reject it; unbelievers regard signs as tricks because they do not reflect.
rows.anchor: قيل الحكمة فيه إلزام الحجة وقطع المعذرة في إظهار الدلائل

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: If other gods existed, they would seek nearness to the Lord of the Throne, recognizing His superiority.
rows.anchor: والتمسوا الزلفة عنده لعلمهم بعلوه عليهم وعظمته عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes say the supposed gods would seek to overpower and contest the Lord; parity among gods would lead to rivalry, the argument from mutual prevention.
rows.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين معناه لطلبوا سبيلا إلى معازة مالك العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above their claims; ʿuluww substitutes for taʿālan, and the Throne is singled out to honor it or may mean sovereignty.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يقل تعاليا كبيرا لأنه وضع مصدر مكان مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creation glorifies God by indicating His unity and justice; created things point to the eternal, self-sufficient maker.
rows.anchor: معنى التسبيح ها هنا الدلالة على توحيد الله وعدله وأنه لا شريك له

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says only living things glorify; Ibrahim and others say even animals, birds, and inanimate things such as a creaking door and flowing water do.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن معناه وما من شيء من الأحياء إلا يسبح بحمده عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fail to understand creation's glorification because they do not contemplate its signs; God delays punishment and forgives those who repent.
rows.anchor: لا تعلمون تسبيح هذه الأشياء حيث لم تنظروا فيها فتعلموا كيف دلالتها
